gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the GardePro Link 1.0 camera cannot join Wi-Fi at all: it talks to its hub over the 802.11ah long-range protocol (Wi-Fi HaLow, which the Wi-Fi Alliance says runs below 1 GHz), and the hub must be wired by Ethernet to a DHCP router. The E8 3.0 Pro and E9 3.0 Pro join a 2.4 GHz home network directly and do not support Live View in that mode, so the camera's distance from the house depends on which radio it uses, not on camera specs.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited pages. The GardePro E8 3.0 Pro overview and the E9 3.0 Pro page say 2.4 GHz and no Live View in Home WiFi mode. They give no router range or security requirements. The E9 product page returned HTTP 429, so I used GardePro's E9 3.0 Pro overview doc instead. Magnolia Trail Camera already says the Link hub 'plugs into your router with an Ethernet cable' and uses its own long-range signal 'rated at about 1,600 feet', and it puts a typical router's outdoor reach at 100–150 ft. None of these pages name 802.11ah or HaLow, say the radio is below 1 GHz, say the R3 camera cannot join Wi-Fi directly, or give the hub's antenna and mounting advice. I also checked itechguides and lenstroop, and neither mentions any of this. Magnolia already gives the practical result, so the new part is the reason behind it.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's split by distance rather than changing the pick. Within a typical router's 2.4 GHz outdoor reach (Magnolia: 100–150 ft in clear line of sight, less through leaves), choose the E8 3.0 Pro or E9 3.0 Pro. Beyond that, choose the Link 1.0. Its camera never uses home Wi-Fi: it uses an 802.11ah link to a wired hub rated 1,600 ft typical. That needs a free Ethernet port on a DHCP router, and it is the only one of the three with remote Live View.
